words.enDefinition: A team or workplace that gathers, edits, and publishes news.

examples.en: The student newsroom moved its planning meeting earlier so reporters could cover the afternoon library opening.
examples.zh: 学生「新闻采编部」把策划会提前，让记者能报道下午的图书馆开馆活动。

examples.en: Our class visited a newsroom and watched editors discuss which stories needed further checks before publication.
examples.zh: 全班参观了一家「新闻采编部」，看到编辑讨论哪些报道在发表前还需要核查。

words.enDefinition: The editorial team coordinating incoming reports and current news coverage.

examples.en: The reporter sent the confirmed timetable to the news desk once the library posted it publicly.
examples.zh: 图书馆公开时间表后，记者把已核实的时间表发给了「新闻编辑台」。

examples.en: The news desk decided which of the two student articles should lead the evening bulletin.
examples.zh: 「新闻编辑台」决定晚上新闻简报的头条应当选两篇学生报道中的哪一篇。

collocations: send updates to the news desk

words.enDefinition: The newsroom team that monitors leads and assigns people to cover events.

examples.en: The assignment desk sent one reporter to the student fair and kept another available for updates.
examples.zh: 「采访调度台」派一名记者去学生集市，并安排另一人随时跟进最新消息。

examples.en: Our mock assignment desk tracked the public meeting schedule while matching each event with available reporters.
examples.zh: 模拟「采访调度台」一边跟踪公开会议日程，一边为各活动安排有空的记者。

collocations: a producer on the assignment desk

words.enDefinition: A newsroom unit responsible for local or municipal news.

examples.en: The city desk assigned the recycling story because several nearby streets would receive new collection schedules.
examples.zh: 因为附近几条街道将启用新的垃圾回收时间表，「城市新闻编辑组」安排了这条报道。

examples.en: The student reporter sent the bus route update to the city desk instead of the features team.
examples.zh: 学生记者把公交线路更新发给「城市新闻编辑组」，没有发给专题报道组。

collocations: a story for the city desk
send copy to the city desk

words.enDefinition: The newsroom unit responsible for checking and preparing written material for publication.

examples.en: The copy desk queried the spelling of a building name before the campus article went online.
examples.zh: 校园报道上线前，「文字编辑台」请记者核实一栋楼的名称拼写。

examples.en: The student paper sent the completed story to the copy desk for a final review.
examples.zh: 学生报把完成的报道送交「文字编辑台」进行最后一次审读。

collocations: send an article to the copy desk
a query from the copy desk

words.enDefinition: An editor overseeing daily operations, staffing, or schedules under the publication's structure.

examples.en: The managing editor moved the student newspaper's deadline after checking when reporters could finish their assignments.
examples.zh: 「执行编辑」问清记者何时能完成采编任务后，调整了学生报的截稿时间。

examples.en: We asked the managing editor how the campus team divided editing work during the busiest publishing week.
examples.zh: 我们问「执行编辑」，在发稿最繁忙的一周，校园媒体小组是怎么分配编辑工作的。

collocations: a decision by the managing editor

words.enDefinition: The senior editor with overall responsibility for a publication's editorial direction.

examples.en: The editor-in-chief approved a new policy on how the student paper would label opinion pieces.
examples.zh: 「总编辑」批准了一项新规定，明确学生报怎样给评论文章加标识。

examples.en: The editorial board sent its proposed coverage priorities to the editor-in-chief before the new term began.
examples.zh: 新学期开始前，编委会把建议优先报道的议题发给了「总编辑」。

words.enDefinition: The editor who tracks emerging stories and assigns reporters or crews.

examples.en: The assignment editor asked a student reporter to cover the open rehearsal while another checked the schedule.
examples.zh: 「采访调度编辑」请一名学生记者报道公开排练，同时让另一人核实日程。

examples.en: We told the assignment editor which two volunteers could attend the afternoon event for the newsroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们告诉「采访调度编辑」，新闻室演练中哪两名志愿者能参加下午的活动。

words.enDefinition: An editor who checks written copy for accuracy, clarity, consistency, and style.

examples.en: The copy editor checked the spelling of building names and the figures in the campus article.
examples.zh: 「文字编辑」核对了校园报道里的建筑名称拼写和数字。

examples.en: Our copy editor flagged a sentence whose pronoun could refer to either person in the interview.
examples.zh: 我们的「文字编辑」标出了一句有歧义的话，其中的代词可能指两位受访者中的任何一位。

collocations: send a draft to a copy editor

words.enDefinition: An editor who selects, oversees, and prepares current news coverage at an outlet.

examples.en: The news editor asked for a second account before approving the student story about the library opening.
examples.zh: 「新闻编辑」要求找另一份说法，再批准关于图书馆开馆的学生报道。

examples.en: Our news editor placed the transport update ahead of the club profile in the afternoon edition.
examples.zh: 在下午版中，我们的「新闻编辑」把交通更新排在社团人物报道之前。

collocations: a decision by the news editor

words.enDefinition: An editor who helps coverage reach and serve readers, viewers, or listeners.

examples.en: The audience editor used questions from readers to suggest topics for the student newsroom's next explainer.
examples.zh: 「受众编辑」根据读者提问，为校园新闻室的下一篇解释性报道提出了选题。

examples.en: Our audience editor suggested publishing the campus transit guide before new students arrived for the term.
examples.zh: 我们的「受众编辑」建议在新生到校前发布校园交通指南。

words.enDefinition: An editor responsible for interpreting and applying a newsroom's editorial standards.

examples.en: The standards editor reviewed whether the draft explained its use of an unnamed source clearly enough.
examples.zh: 「新闻规范编辑」审查了草稿是否充分说明采用匿名消息来源的原因。

examples.en: We asked the standards editor how the fictional newsroom should describe the mistake in its notice.
examples.zh: 我们问「新闻规范编辑」，虚构新闻室应怎样在公告里说明这处错误。

collocations: a review by the standards editor

words.enDefinition: A reporter regularly assigned to cover a particular subject, institution, or area.

examples.en: The campus beat reporter followed every public meeting about changes to the library's opening hours.
examples.zh: 负责校园新闻的「条线记者」跟踪了关于调整图书馆开放时间的每一次公开会议。

examples.en: Our class interviewed a beat reporter who regularly covered local transit planning and service changes.
examples.zh: 全班采访了一名经常报道本地交通规划和服务调整的「条线记者」。

words.enDefinition: A reporter employed as part of a publication's regular staff.

examples.en: The staff reporter took over the follow-up when the freelance contributor finished the first article.
examples.zh: 自由撰稿人完成首篇文章后，「媒体在职记者」接手了后续报道。

examples.en: The student newsroom listed its staff reporter beside the editor on the contact page for readers.
examples.zh: 学生新闻室在面向读者的联系页面上，把「媒体在职记者」列在编辑旁边。

collocations: a story by a staff reporter

words.enDefinition: A self-employed reporter who contributes work to publications without a regular staff position there.

examples.en: The magazine commissioned a freelance reporter to cover the campus book fair for its local section.
examples.zh: 杂志约请一名「自由记者」为地方新闻版报道校园书展。

examples.en: The freelance reporter sent the student editor two sample stories before discussing the proposed assignment.
examples.zh: 这名「自由记者」先给学生编辑发了两篇报道样稿，随后讨论拟定的采访任务。

words.enDefinition: A freelance contributor who supplies coverage to an outlet as needed, often from a particular locality.

examples.en: The regional desk asked its local stringer to cover a meeting the staff could not attend.
examples.zh: 地区新闻组请当地「特约供稿记者」去报道一场本部记者无法参加的会议。

examples.en: The student publication credited a stringer who regularly sent short reports from the second campus.
examples.zh: 学生刊物在报道上注明一名「特约供稿记者」的姓名，此人经常从第二校区发来简讯。

words.enDefinition: A journalist assigned by a news organization to report from a particular location or region.

examples.en: The outlet's news correspondent filed a report from the town where the student debate took place.
examples.zh: 这家媒体的「驻地记者」从学生辩论比赛举行的小城发回了报道。

examples.en: Our class compared the news correspondent's account with a summary prepared by editors back at headquarters.
examples.zh: 全班把「驻地记者」的报道与总部编辑编写的摘要作比较。

collocations: a report from a news correspondent

words.enDefinition: A service distributing news reports or other material to subscriber outlets.

examples.en: The student editor checked the wire service for updates before revising the regional news roundup.
examples.zh: 学生编辑在修改地区新闻综述之前，先查了「通讯社供稿服务」里的最新报道。

examples.en: Our exercise used a fictional wire service to show how several newspapers could receive the same report.
examples.zh: 练习用虚构的「通讯社供稿服务」展示多家报纸如何收到同一篇稿件。

collocations: a report from a wire service

words.enDefinition: A branch office maintaining reporting coverage of a particular location or region.

examples.en: The fictional newspaper assigned two reporters to its news bureau near the second campus.
examples.zh: 虚构报社派两名记者到第二校区附近的「新闻驻地机构」工作。

examples.en: Our class examined how the news bureau kept the central desk informed about events in its area.
examples.zh: 全班考察了「新闻驻地机构」如何向总部编辑台通报当地的各项动态。

words.enDefinition: A meeting at which editors and reporters plan coverage and discuss stories.

examples.en: At the editorial meeting, student reporters explained which sources they had reached and what remained unconfirmed.
examples.zh: 在「编采会议」上，学生记者说明已经联系了哪些消息来源，还有哪些细节没有确认。

examples.en: The editorial meeting ended with a schedule for the two stories the newsroom wanted by Friday.
examples.zh: 「编采会议」结束时，新闻室定下时间表，要求周五前完成两篇报道。

collocations: bring a pitch to an editorial meeting

words.enDefinition: A reporter's proposal to an editor explaining an idea, its significance, and how to report it.

examples.en: The student editor accepted the story pitch because it identified a timely question and possible sources.
examples.zh: 学生编辑接受了这份「新闻选题提案」，因为它找准了一个当前值得报道的问题，并列出可能的消息来源。

examples.en: We revised the story pitch after realizing the original idea was too broad for one article.
examples.zh: 我们意识到原来的构想太宽，一篇报道写不下，就修改了「新闻选题提案」。

words.enDefinition: A particular piece of coverage assigned to a reporter or reporting team.

examples.en: Her first story assignment was to interview the organizers and verify the schedule for the campus festival.
examples.zh: 她的首个「报道任务」是采访组织人员，并核实校园节日活动的日程。

examples.en: The editor shared the story assignment with two students who could attend different parts of the meeting.
examples.zh: 编辑把「报道任务」分给两名学生，两人可以分别旁听会议的不同环节。

collocations: give a reporter a story assignment

words.enDefinition: A newsroom planning list of proposed or scheduled coverage for a publication period.

examples.en: The story budget listed each planned article with its deadline and expected length for the next issue.
examples.zh: 「报道计划清单」列出下一期准备刊登的每篇报道及其截稿时间和预计篇幅。

examples.en: We checked the story budget before promising a second article about the same campus event.
examples.zh: 我们先看了「报道计划清单」，再答应就同一校园活动再写一篇报道。

collocations: add an item to the story budget

words.enDefinition: A short identifier used to label a story in an editorial workflow.

examples.en: The story slug identified the library article while editors were still deciding on its public headline.
examples.zh: 编辑还在商量对外刊登的标题时，用「稿件内部简称」标识这篇图书馆报道。

examples.en: We kept the same story slug when the headline changed because the assignment itself stayed the same.
examples.zh: 由于报道任务本身没变，修改标题时我们沿用了原来的「稿件内部简称」。

words.enDefinition: The latest time written material must be submitted for editorial processing.

examples.en: The copy deadline gave student editors an hour to check the facts before the newsletter went out.
examples.zh: 按「文稿截稿时间」收稿后，学生编辑在发简报前还有一小时可核对事实。

examples.en: We asked for an earlier copy deadline because the mock edition included several stories needing extra review.
examples.zh: 模拟刊物有好几篇稿件需要加审，我们因此要求提前「文稿截稿时间」。

words.enDefinition: To send a completed news report to an editor or newsroom system.

examples.en: The student reporter planned to file a story once she had checked when the exhibition would open.
examples.zh: 学生记者打算核实展览的开幕时间后再「提交报道稿」。

examples.en: We practiced how to file a story with a clear slug and a complete list of sources.
examples.zh: 我们练习如何「提交报道稿」，随稿附上好辨认的稿件简称和完整的消息来源清单。

collocations: file a story from the scene
file a story for the evening edition

words.enDefinition: To check and revise text for clarity, accuracy, consistency, grammar, or house style.

examples.en: The volunteer agreed to copy edit the campus story after the reporter verified the event details.
examples.zh: 志愿者同意等记者核实活动细节后，「校订」这篇校园报道。

examples.en: We learned to copy edit the newsletter without changing what the quoted students had originally said.
examples.zh: 我们练习如何「校订」这份简报，同时保留受访学生原来的表述。

collocations: copy edit a draft before publication

words.enDefinition: To revise a text sentence by sentence for flow, precision, and expression.

examples.en: The editor asked us to line edit a paragraph whose main point was buried in long sentences.
examples.zh: 有一段的主旨被长句埋没了，编辑请我们对这段话「逐句润色」。

examples.en: We had time to line edit the feature after settling how its three sections should fit together.
examples.zh: 理顺专题报道三个部分之间的关系后，我们有时间进行「逐句润色」。

collocations: line edit an article for clarity

words.enDefinition: To decide that a prepared or proposed news story will not be published.

examples.en: The editor chose to spike a story when its central claim could not be verified for the issue.
examples.zh: 那期刊物截稿前没能核实稿件的核心说法，编辑决定「撤下待发报道」。

examples.en: Our classroom exercise asked what would justify a decision to spike a story after extensive reporting.
examples.zh: 课堂练习问，做了大量采访工作后，什么理由足以让编辑决定「撤下待发报道」。

collocations: a decision to spike a story

words.enDefinition: To delay publication of a report pending more information or a decision.

examples.en: The editor agreed to hold a story until the reporter could confirm the new timetable in writing.
examples.zh: 编辑同意「暂缓刊发报道」，等记者以书面材料确认新的时间表。

examples.en: We chose to hold a story for another day rather than publish the date without checking it.
examples.zh: 我们决定再等一天，「暂缓刊发报道」，免得贸然公布尚未核实的日期。

collocations: hold a story until details are confirmed

words.enDefinition: Written news material distributed by a wire service for publication use.

examples.en: The student editor compared the wire copy with the local reporter's notes before writing a short update.
examples.zh: 学生编辑写简短更新前，把「通讯社供稿」与当地记者的笔记作了比较。

examples.en: The regional paper used wire copy for the opening summary and added its own campus interviews.
examples.zh: 地区报纸用「通讯社供稿」写开头摘要，同时加入了自己做的校园采访。

words.enDefinition: An outlet's use or publication of material supplied by a wire service.

examples.en: The instructor used wire pickup to explain why identical regional reports appeared in several fictional newspapers.
examples.zh: 老师用「转载通讯社稿件」解释了为什么几家虚构报纸会刊登内容相同的地区报道。

examples.en: We noted the wire pickup after finding the wire service credit on the regional news website.
examples.zh: 看到地区新闻网站注明稿件来自通讯社之后，我们记录了这次「转载通讯社稿件」的情况。

collocations: a wire pickup by a local newspaper

words.enDefinition: Distributing the same article or regular feature for publication by multiple outlets.

examples.en: The case used news syndication to show how the same student column ran in three local papers.
examples.zh: 案例用「新闻稿件联供」说明同一篇学生专栏是怎么在三家当地报纸上刊登的。

examples.en: We discussed news syndication after the fictional publisher considered offering its weekly column to other outlets.
examples.zh: 虚构发行方考虑向其他媒体供应自己的每周专栏后，我们讨论了「新闻稿件联供」。

words.enDefinition: The space available for editorial content in a print publication after other allocations.

examples.en: The printed issue had a smaller news hole after the bookstore advertisement took half a page.
examples.zh: 书店广告占了半页，这期纸质刊物的「新闻可用版面」变小了。

examples.en: Our class shortened two articles to fit the news hole in the simulated campus edition.
examples.zh: 全班缩短了两篇文章，以适应模拟校园刊物的「新闻可用版面」。

collocations: fit a story into the news hole

words.enDefinition: A coordinated set of related news pieces or materials published together.

examples.en: The newsroom assembled a story package with a main article, a timeline, and a short explainer.
examples.zh: 新闻室组建了「成套报道」，包括主稿、时间线和一篇简短的解释性报道。

examples.en: Our student team built a story package around the new bus route instead of relying on one article.
examples.zh: 学生小组围绕公交新线路组织了「成套报道」，用多篇内容来呈现。

collocations: a story package on a local issue

words.enDefinition: Timely fact-focused reporting on developments with immediate or substantial public significance.

examples.en: The instructor treated the library's sudden closure as hard news because it affected students that day.
examples.zh: 老师把图书馆突然关闭作为「硬新闻」，因为这件事当天就影响到学生。

examples.en: We placed hard news about service changes ahead of the campus gardening feature in the sample edition.
examples.zh: 在样刊中，我们把关于服务调整的「硬新闻」排在校园园艺特写前面。

words.enDefinition: Reporting centered on lifestyle, personal experience, or human interest rather than urgent public developments.

examples.en: The editor grouped the piece about students' favorite reading corners with the magazine's other soft news.
examples.zh: 编辑把介绍学生最喜欢的阅读角的文章归入杂志的其他「软新闻」。

examples.en: We compared soft news in the weekend section with the urgent transport reports on the front page.
examples.zh: 我们把周末版的「软新闻」与头版的紧急交通报道作比较。

words.enDefinition: A fact-focused account of an event that keeps interpretation and personal opinion separate.

examples.en: The campus paper published a straight news report summarizing the library board's decision and its starting date.
examples.zh: 校园报发表了一篇「直述新闻报道」，概述图书馆委员会的决定及生效日期。

examples.en: Our class turned the student writer's notes into a straight news report rather than an opinion column.
examples.zh: 全班把学生作者的笔记写成「直述新闻报道」，没有写成评论专栏。

collocations: the lead of a straight news report

words.enDefinition: A short report stating the essential facts about one development.

examples.en: The news brief gave the new opening time and told students which entrance would remain available.
examples.zh: 「简讯」提供了新的开放时间，还告诉学生哪个入口依然开放。

examples.en: We wrote a news brief first because readers needed the basic transport information before the longer article.
examples.zh: 我们先写「简讯」，因为读者在看到长篇报道之前就需要基本交通信息。

collocations: include an item in a news brief

words.enDefinition: A short notification sent when a significant development has just become known.

examples.en: The student newsroom sent a breaking news alert after confirming that the main library would close early.
examples.zh: 校园新闻室确认总图书馆会提前关闭后，发出了一条「突发新闻快讯」。

examples.en: The editor checked the breaking news alert against the public statement before sending it to readers.
examples.zh: 编辑发给读者之前，核对了「突发新闻快讯」是否与公开声明相符。

words.enDefinition: A news story about a situation whose relevant facts are still emerging.

examples.en: The bus route proposal remained a developing story because the council had yet to publish its timetable.
examples.zh: 公交路线提案仍是「持续发展的新闻」，因为委员会尚未公布时间表。

examples.en: We distinguished confirmed facts from missing details when updating the developing story in our classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 在课堂练习中更新「持续发展的新闻」时，我们区分了已确认的事实和仍待了解的细节。

words.enDefinition: A later report adding developments or consequences to an issue previously covered.

examples.en: The student editor requested a follow-up story after the first week of the library's longer opening hours.
examples.zh: 图书馆延长开放时间满一周后，学生编辑要求做一篇「跟进报道」。

examples.en: Our follow-up story asked whether the promised timetable had actually been posted on the campus noticeboard.
examples.zh: 我们的「跟进报道」查问了公告栏上是不是真的贴出了先前承诺的时间表。

collocations: an idea for a follow-up story

words.enDefinition: A single report summarizing several related news developments.

examples.en: The weekly news roundup summarized several campus announcements that students might have missed during exam week.
examples.zh: 每周「新闻综览」汇总了几条学生可能在考试周漏看的校园公告。

examples.en: We arranged the news roundup by subject so readers could find transport updates without scanning every item.
examples.zh: 我们按主题编排「新闻综览」，读者无须逐条查看就能找到交通更新。

words.enDefinition: A companion news piece presenting a focused aspect of a larger main report.

examples.en: The sidebar story explained the free shuttle route that the main article could only mention briefly.
examples.zh: 「主稿配发短文」详细介绍了主稿只能简短提及的免费接驳车路线。

examples.en: Our editor assigned a sidebar story about the timetable and saved the policy debate for the main report.
examples.zh: 编辑安排了介绍时间表的「主稿配发短文」，有关政策的讨论则留在主稿。

words.enDefinition: A reported article developing a subject through detail, context, or narrative.

examples.en: The news feature used interviews with several student gardeners to explain how the shared plot had developed.
examples.zh: 这篇「新闻特写」采访了几名参与园艺的学生，说明共享种植区的发展过程。

examples.en: We expanded the news feature after finding earlier records that explained why the project began.
examples.zh: 找到能解释项目缘起的早期记录后，我们扩充了「新闻特写」。

words.enDefinition: A report focusing on personal experiences that give a topic emotional or human significance.

examples.en: The human-interest story focused on how two students built a friendship through volunteering at the library.
examples.zh: 这篇「人情故事报道」聚焦两名学生如何在图书馆做志愿服务时建立友谊。

examples.en: The editor asked us to base the human-interest story on reported details from the students' own accounts.
examples.zh: 编辑要求我们根据学生亲口讲述的细节来写「人情故事报道」。

words.enDefinition: Reporting that interprets developments using evidence and context beyond the basic facts.

examples.en: The news analysis compared earlier transport decisions to explain why the new route mattered to commuters.
examples.zh: 这篇「新闻分析」比较以往交通决定，解释新线路为什么对通勤者重要。

examples.en: We labeled the article news analysis because it interpreted the evidence instead of merely summarizing the announcement.
examples.zh: 文章解读了证据，超出了概述公告的范围，所以我们将它标为「新闻分析」。

words.enDefinition: An article making a complex topic understandable by answering key questions and supplying context.

examples.en: The student paper published an explainer article about how the new library reservation system would work.
examples.zh: 学生报发了一篇「解释性报道」，说明图书馆新的预约系统如何运作。

examples.en: We built the explainer article around three questions readers had asked after seeing the initial announcement.
examples.zh: 我们围绕读者看过最初公告后提出的三个问题写成了「解释性报道」。

words.enDefinition: Reporting that gives readers practical information they can use in everyday decisions.

examples.en: The transport guide was service journalism because readers could use it to choose a campus bus route.
examples.zh: 交通指南属于「实用服务新闻」，读者可以据此选择校园公交线路。

examples.en: The class discussed service journalism after comparing two guides to using the library's public study rooms.
examples.zh: 全班比较两份图书馆公共自习室使用指南后，讨论了「实用服务新闻」。

words.enDefinition: In-depth reporting that systematically uncovers significant facts not already apparent to the public.

examples.en: The simulated investigative reporting project compared public records to explain why library repairs had been repeatedly delayed.
examples.zh: 模拟「调查性报道」项目对照公开记录，解释了图书馆维修为什么一再延迟。

examples.en: Our instructor emphasized that investigative reporting needed documentary evidence and fair responses from those discussed.
examples.zh: 老师强调，「调查性报道」需要有文件证据，并给报道中涉及的各方公平回应的机会。

words.enDefinition: Reporter-initiated coverage that develops an original story beyond routine events or announcements.

examples.en: The enterprise reporting assignment began with questions from readers rather than with a scheduled campus announcement.
examples.zh: 「记者主动策划的报道」作业从读者的提问出发，并非由一次预定的校园公告发起。

examples.en: We discussed enterprise reporting after a reporter connected several small library changes into one original story.
examples.zh: 一名记者把图书馆数项小调整串成一篇原创报道后，我们讨论了「记者主动策划的报道」。

words.enDefinition: Regular reporting on an assigned topic, institution, or geographic area.

examples.en: The class practiced beat reporting by following campus transport decisions across several consecutive public meetings.
examples.zh: 课堂通过连续跟踪几次公开会议中的校园交通决策，练习「条线报道」。

examples.en: We compared beat reporting with a single assignment about the library's annual book sale.
examples.zh: 我们把「条线报道」与图书馆一年一度图书义卖的一次性报道任务作比较。

words.enDefinition: Coverage of government bodies, public institutions, and decisions affecting a community.

examples.en: The public affairs reporting exercise asked students to explain how a council decision changed local library hours.
examples.zh: 「公共事务报道」练习要求学生说明，某项委员会决定怎样改变了当地图书馆的开放时间。

examples.en: We used a public meeting summary to practice public affairs reporting with clearly attributed statements.
examples.zh: 我们用一份公开会议摘要练习「公共事务报道」，并清楚标明每项说法的来源。

collocations: a course in public affairs reporting
public affairs reporting on local services

words.enDefinition: An online page updated frequently with brief entries as an event unfolds.

examples.en: The student newsroom ran a liveblog during the public workshop with times attached to every update.
examples.zh: 校园新闻室在公开工作坊期间维护了一个「实时滚动报道页」，每次更新都标出了时间。

examples.en: We checked the liveblog for a short summary after missing the first part of the meeting.
examples.zh: 错过会议开头后，我们查看「实时滚动报道页」，寻找简短摘要。

words.enDefinition: A signed opinion article, often contributed by someone outside a publication's editorial board.

examples.en: The student paper published an op-ed in which a librarian argued for keeping the reading room open later.
examples.zh: 学生报刊登了一篇「署名评论文章」，一名图书管理员在文中主张延长阅览室开放时间。

examples.en: Our editor labeled the piece an op-ed to make its argument distinct from the day's news coverage.
examples.zh: 编辑把这篇文章标为「署名评论文章」，让读者能将文章观点与当天新闻报道区分开。

words.enDefinition: The group responsible for developing a publication's collective positions on matters addressed in its editorials.

examples.en: The editorial board discussed the student paper's opinion policy before publishing its statement about campus services.
examples.zh: 学生报的「编辑委员会」在发布有关校园服务的声明之前，先讨论了评论版的方针。

examples.en: We asked the editorial board how its collective views were distinguished from those of individual columnists.
examples.zh: 我们问「编辑委员会」，怎样区分委员会集体观点和专栏作者的个人观点。

collocations: a decision by the editorial board

words.enDefinition: A recurring signed article series in which a writer presents personal argument or interpretation.

examples.en: The weekly opinion column discussed study spaces from the writer's own perspective and cited several public reports.
examples.zh: 每周「评论专栏」从作者个人角度讨论学习空间，并引用了几份公开报告。

examples.en: We marked the opinion column clearly so readers knew whose argument they were reading in the newspaper.
examples.zh: 我们为「评论专栏」加上清楚的标识，让读者在报纸上读到观点时知道作者是谁。

words.enDefinition: A current event or development that makes a topic timely to report now.

examples.en: The publication of a new bus timetable gave our article about campus transport a clear news peg.
examples.zh: 新公交时间表的发布，为我们的校园交通报道提供了明确的「新闻由头」。

examples.en: The editor asked for a news peg because the same library issue had existed for years.
examples.zh: 图书馆的同一个问题已存在多年，编辑要求找一个当下的「新闻由头」。

collocations: use a development as a news peg

words.enDefinition: The specific aspect or perspective that guides how a news story is reported.

examples.en: The team chose a news angle focused on how the plan would affect students who commute.
examples.zh: 小组选择的「新闻报道角度」是这项计划如何影响通勤学生。

examples.en: We changed the news angle after interviews showed that evening access mattered more than the new building.
examples.zh: 采访发现晚间能否使用设施比新建筑更重要，于是我们调整了「新闻报道角度」。

words.enDefinition: The opening of a news story designed to present key facts or draw readers in.

examples.en: The reporter rewrote the lede after learning that the new library hours would begin a week earlier.
examples.zh: 记者得知图书馆的新开放时间会提前一周启用后，重写了「新闻导语」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the lede told readers what had changed before introducing the detailed background.
examples.zh: 老师问，「新闻导语」是否在介绍详细背景之前已经告诉读者具体变了什么。

words.enDefinition: A story opening stating the most important verified facts immediately.

examples.en: The summary lead gave the reopening date, location, and reason for the delay in one concise paragraph.
examples.zh: 「概述式导语」用简练的一段交代了重新开放日期、地点和延误原因。

examples.en: We used a summary lead because readers needed the confirmed timetable before any personal accounts.
examples.zh: 我们采用「概述式导语」，因为读者需要先看到核实后的时间表，再读个人讲述。

words.enDefinition: An opening that begins with a short reported anecdote related to the larger story.

examples.en: The anecdotal lead described a student's first library visit before the article explained wider attendance changes.
examples.zh: 「轶事式导语」描述了一名学生第一次去图书馆的经历，报道随后解释了整体到访量的变化。

examples.en: We checked whether the anecdotal lead illustrated the central issue rather than simply opening with a pleasant detail.
examples.zh: 我们核查「轶事式导语」是否体现了核心问题，避免只以一段趣事开头。

words.enDefinition: An opening that sets a scene or creates interest before stating the central news point later.

examples.en: The feature used a delayed lead to set the scene before revealing why the afternoon workshop mattered.
examples.zh: 专题采用「延宕式导语」先交代现场，再点明下午这场工作坊为什么值得报道。

examples.en: Our class compared a delayed lead with an opening that stated the council's decision immediately.
examples.zh: 课堂把「延宕式导语」与直接开头交代委员会决定的写法作比较。

collocations: a feature with a delayed lead

words.enDefinition: An early paragraph explaining what the story is about and why it matters.

examples.en: The nut graf connected one student's experience with the wider changes in evening access across campus.
examples.zh: 「点题段」把一名学生的经历与校园晚间开放安排的整体变化联系起来。

examples.en: We moved the nut graf higher so readers would understand the significance before reaching the interview details.
examples.zh: 我们把「点题段」移到更前面，让读者在看到采访细节前就能明白报道的意义。

words.enDefinition: A news structure putting essential facts first and arranging later details by decreasing importance.

examples.en: The student wrote in an inverted pyramid so the opening carried the most important timetable changes.
examples.zh: 这名学生运用「倒金字塔结构」，在开头交代最重要的时间表改动。

examples.en: We compared the inverted pyramid with a feature structure that revealed key information more gradually.
examples.zh: 我们把「倒金字塔结构」与逐步披露关键信息的特写写法作比较。

collocations: write in the inverted pyramid format

words.enDefinition: A published credit identifying who wrote or reported a story.

examples.en: The editor added a shared byline after both students contributed interviews and wrote parts of the story.
examples.zh: 两名学生都参与了采访和写作，编辑加上了共同的「记者署名」。

examples.en: We checked the byline before citing the article because several people had worked on the edition.
examples.zh: 由于有几个人参与制作那期刊物，我们先核对「记者署名」再引用该文。

words.enDefinition: A line at the start of a news report identifying its place of origin and sometimes its date.

examples.en: The dateline named the town where the reporter gathered the information for the local transport story.
examples.zh: 「新闻电头」标出了记者为当地交通报道采集信息的城镇。

examples.en: Our editor checked the dateline before publication because the story drew on reporting from two locations.
examples.zh: 因为稿件取材于两个地点的采访，编辑在发表前核对了「新闻电头」。

collocations: a dateline at the start of a report

words.enDefinition: A short line directing readers to where a printed story continues.

examples.en: The jump line directed readers from the front page to the rest of the story on page four.
examples.zh: 「续版提示行」指引读者从头版跳到第四版，继续阅读余下内容。

examples.en: We corrected the jump line after the final pages of the student newspaper were rearranged.
examples.zh: 学生报的后几版重新编排后，我们更正了「续版提示行」。

words.enDefinition: An excerpt from an article displayed prominently to catch the reader's attention.

examples.en: The layout editor selected a pull quote from the article to highlight one student's description of the library.
examples.zh: 版面编辑选了文章中一名学生对图书馆的描述，做成一段「突出显示的引文」。

examples.en: We checked that the pull quote matched the article and did not change the speaker's meaning.
examples.zh: 我们核对「突出显示的引文」是否与正文一致，确保没有改变说话者本意。

collocations: display a pull quote alongside the story

words.enDefinition: The degree to which an event or issue deserves coverage according to journalistic criteria.

examples.en: The tutor explained newsworthiness by asking how many readers would be affected by the timetable change.
examples.zh: 辅导老师通过询问会有多少读者受到时间表调整影响来解释「新闻报道价值」。

examples.en: We debated the newsworthiness of two campus topics before selecting one for the class assignment.
examples.zh: 全班在选择作业选题前，讨论了两个校园议题的「新闻报道价值」。

collocations: discuss the newsworthiness of a story

words.enDefinition: The ability to decide what deserves coverage and how prominently it should appear.

examples.en: The editor used news judgment to place the library closure above the story about new shelves.
examples.zh: 编辑运用「新闻判断力」，把图书馆关闭的新闻排在介绍新书架的稿件前面。

examples.en: Our class discussed news judgment after two groups independently selected different stories for the front page.
examples.zh: 两个小组各自选出了不同的头版报道后，全班讨论了「新闻判断力」。

words.enDefinition: Identifying a source by name when reporting their information or words.

examples.en: The editor used named attribution for the timetable explanation after the librarian agreed to be quoted.
examples.zh: 图书管理员同意被引用后，编辑对这段时间表说明采用了「具名归因」。

examples.en: We checked that named attribution in the draft gave the speaker's approved name and relevant position.
examples.zh: 我们核对草稿中的「具名归因」是否使用了说话者确认的姓名，并注明与报道相关的职务。

collocations: write a sentence with named attribution
seek named attribution for a claim

words.enDefinition: Attributing information to a source using a description without publishing their name.

examples.en: The instructor asked whether anonymous attribution gave readers enough context to assess how the source knew.
examples.zh: 老师问，「匿名归因」是否给了读者足够的背景来判断消息来源是怎么知道这件事的。

examples.en: In the exercise, anonymous attribution described the source's role without identifying them in the published story.
examples.zh: 练习中，报道采用「匿名归因」，说明消息来源的身份角色，没有公开其姓名。

words.enDefinition: A verb connecting information or quoted words to their stated source.

examples.en: Our copy editor replaced an attribution verb that implied doubt without evidence supporting that interpretation.
examples.zh: 在没有证据支持质疑时，文字编辑换掉了会让人以为消息存疑的「归因动词」。

examples.en: The class compared each attribution verb to see how it changed the tone of the reported remark.
examples.zh: 全班比较各个「归因动词」，查看它们怎样改变转述内容的语气。

collocations: an attribution verb in a quotation

words.enDefinition: A phrase beside a quotation identifying who supplied its words or information.

examples.en: The student reporter added an attribution tag after the quotation to make the speaker's identity clear.
examples.zh: 学生记者在引语后加了「引语出处标记」，让读者清楚是谁说的话。

examples.en: We moved the attribution tag earlier because two people were quoted in the same paragraph.
examples.zh: 因同一段引用了两个人的话，我们把「引语出处标记」移到更前面。

collocations: an attribution tag after a quotation

words.enDefinition: Restating what someone said without presenting it as their exact words.

examples.en: The reader could tell from the reported speech that the writer was summarizing the organizer's explanation.
examples.zh: 读者从「间接引语」看出，作者是在概述组织人员的解释。

examples.en: We used reported speech for the routine details and reserved quotation marks for the librarian's exact words.
examples.zh: 我们用「间接引语」转述常规细节，只给图书管理员的原话加引号。

collocations: convert a quotation into reported speech
distinguish reported speech from direct quotation

words.enDefinition: A short, exact portion of someone's words quoted within a larger sentence.

examples.en: The draft used a partial quotation around the speaker's distinctive phrase rather than the whole answer.
examples.zh: 草稿只给说话者有辨识度的短语加了「部分引语」，没有全文照引回答。

examples.en: We checked the partial quotation against the transcript to make sure the excerpt had kept its meaning.
examples.zh: 我们对照文字记录核查「部分引语」，确保摘出的文字仍保留原意。

collocations: weave a partial quotation into the text

words.enDefinition: A brief excerpt of recorded speech selected for a news report.

examples.en: The radio report included a sound bite in which the librarian explained the new opening hours.
examples.zh: 电台报道采用了一段「新闻采访短引语」，图书管理员在里面解释了新的开放时间。

examples.en: We listened to the full answer before choosing a sound bite for the student news bulletin.
examples.zh: 我们先听完整回答，再为学生新闻简报挑选一段「新闻采访短引语」。

collocations: include a sound bite in a report

words.enDefinition: Available for publication with the source identified, under the agreed interview terms.

examples.en: The organizer spoke on the record, so the article could name her when quoting the opening date.
examples.zh: 组织人员的发言「可具名公开引用」，因此文章引用开幕日期时可以写出她的姓名。

examples.en: The student reporter checked which comments were on the record before drafting the campus news brief.
examples.zh: 学生记者在起草校园简讯前，核实了哪些评论「可具名公开引用」。

collocations: confirm a statement on the record

words.enDefinition: Available for publication under agreed attribution conditions that ordinarily withhold the source's name.

examples.en: The classroom example described comments given on background with an agreed description of the source's role.
examples.zh: 课堂示例中，有些发言「可报道但按约定归因」，文中使用双方商定的方式描述来源的角色。

examples.en: We distinguished a statement offered on background from one the fictional report could attribute by name.
examples.zh: 我们将「可报道但按约定归因」的说法与可在虚构稿件中具名归因的发言作比较。

words.enDefinition: An agreed interview arrangement allowing information to be used without any attribution.

examples.en: The worksheet explained that information shared on deep background could be reported without attribution to the speaker.
examples.zh: 习题说明，「可用但不注明来源」约定允许报道所提供的信息，无须指明谁提供了消息。

examples.en: The instructor compared deep background with an arrangement that allowed the publication to describe the source.
examples.zh: 老师把「可用但不注明来源」与允许媒体描述来源身份的约定作比较。

words.enDefinition: Agreed terms about recording and how information from an interview may be published or attributed.

examples.en: The mock interviewer confirmed the interview ground rules before asking whether the speaker's name could be published.
examples.zh: 模拟采访者先确定「采访引用约定」，再向说话者核对能否公开其姓名。

examples.en: In class, we compared interview ground rules for a recorded statement and a named quotation.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们比较了采访录音和具名引语各自的「采访引用约定」。

words.enDefinition: A source identified by name in a published account.

examples.en: The story used a named source who could confirm when the new library schedule would begin.
examples.zh: 这篇报道采用了「实名消息来源」的消息，对方能够确认图书馆何时启用新的开放安排。

examples.en: The editor asked whether the named source had personally attended the meeting mentioned in the draft.
examples.zh: 编辑问，「实名消息来源」是否亲自参加过草稿中提到的会议。

words.enDefinition: A person who provides information while their name is withheld from publication.

examples.en: The fictional article explained why the anonymous source knew about the meeting without giving the source's name.
examples.zh: 虚构报道解释了「匿名消息来源」为什么了解这场会议，同时没有公开对方的姓名。

examples.en: The editor asked for a second account before accepting the anonymous source's central claim in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，编辑要求取得另一份说法，再接受「匿名消息来源」的核心陈述。

words.enDefinition: Someone with direct experience or direct knowledge of the matter being reported.

examples.en: The librarian was a firsthand source because she attended the meeting where the schedule was approved.
examples.zh: 这名图书管理员是「第一手消息来源」，因为她参加了批准时间表的会议。

examples.en: Our reporter checked whether the firsthand source had actually seen the event described in the draft.
examples.zh: 记者核对「第一手消息来源」是否确实看到了草稿所述的事件。

collocations: verify a claim with a firsthand source

words.enDefinition: A description based on information received from someone else rather than from direct experience.

examples.en: The reporter treated the message as a secondhand account because its writer had not attended the workshop.
examples.zh: 消息的撰写者没有参加工作坊，记者将它当作「转述所得的陈述」。

examples.en: We checked the secondhand account against a public record before including it in the campus article.
examples.zh: 在校园报道中采用这份「转述所得的陈述」之前，我们用公开记录作了核对。

collocations: compare a secondhand account with direct evidence

words.enDefinition: A statement describing an event from someone who personally saw it happen.

examples.en: The student reporter compared each eyewitness account of the power cut with the building's published update.
examples.zh: 学生记者将停电的各份「目击者陈述」分别与大楼发布的最新消息作比较。

examples.en: We checked where the observer stood before relying on the eyewitness account in the simulated report.
examples.zh: 在模拟报道中采用这份「目击者陈述」前，我们先核对观察者当时站在什么位置。

words.enDefinition: A source whose information does not come from the same origin as another account being checked.

examples.en: The newsroom wanted an independent source because the two initial accounts quoted the same public announcement.
examples.zh: 两个最初的说法引用同一份公开公告，新闻室因此想找一个「独立消息来源」。

examples.en: We asked whether the second interview supplied an independent source or merely repeated the first account.
examples.zh: 我们问，第二次采访是否提供了「独立消息来源」，还是只重复了第一个说法。

collocations: confirm a detail with an independent source

words.enDefinition: Assessing a source's credibility, access to information, and relevant interests before using their account.

examples.en: The editor required source vetting before relying on a contributor who claimed to know the timetable.
examples.zh: 一名投稿人称自己知道时间表，编辑要求先做「消息来源审查」，再决定是否采用。

examples.en: Our exercise separated source vetting from checking the dates that the fictional source had provided.
examples.zh: 练习把「消息来源审查」与核对虚构消息提供者给出的日期分开。

words.enDefinition: Separate evidence confirming a report without simply repeating its original source.

examples.en: The public schedule provided independent corroboration of what the workshop organizer had told the reporter.
examples.zh: 公开日程为工作坊组织人员告诉记者的内容提供了「独立佐证」。

examples.en: We waited for independent corroboration after discovering that several posts repeated one person's unverified account.
examples.zh: 发现几条帖子都在转述同一个人的未经核实的说法后，我们决定等到有「独立佐证」再发。

collocations: publish a claim after independent corroboration

words.enDefinition: A newsroom policy requiring two sufficiently independent sources for specified information before publication.

examples.en: The fictional newsroom applied its two-source rule before publishing a claim about the library's opening date.
examples.zh: 虚构新闻室在发表图书馆开放日期这一消息之前，使用了自己的「双来源核实规则」。

examples.en: We discussed why repeating one statement in two outlets did not satisfy the classroom two-source rule.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么两个媒体重复同一份声明，并不能满足课堂的「双来源核实规则」。

words.enDefinition: Explaining relevant information about a source so readers can judge how it supports the story.

examples.en: The article's source disclosure explained that one quoted person helped organize the event under discussion.
examples.zh: 报道中的「消息来源说明」说明，被引用的一个人参与了文中活动的组织工作。

examples.en: We read the source disclosure to see which details about the speaker's role were public.
examples.zh: 我们阅读了「消息来源说明」，查看发言者哪些与报道相关的背景信息已经公开。

words.enDefinition: The opportunity for a person or organization criticized in a report to respond to the relevant claims.

examples.en: Before publication, the editor offered a right of reply to the people criticized in the fictional article.
examples.zh: 刊发前，编辑给虚构报道中受到批评的人提供了「回应权」。

examples.en: Our class discussed whether the right of reply gave the organization enough time to address the concerns.
examples.zh: 全班讨论，报道是否为有关机构充分行使「回应权」留出了时间。

collocations: an opportunity under a right of reply

words.enDefinition: A journalist's invitation for a story subject to address specific claims or questions before publication.

examples.en: The reporter sent a request for comment outlining the questions about the library's revised timetable.
examples.zh: 记者发出了「征询置评请求」，列明有关图书馆调整时间表的问题。

examples.en: The draft noted when the request for comment was sent and whether an answer had arrived.
examples.zh: 草稿注明何时发出「征询置评请求」，以及是否已经收到答复。

collocations: respond to a request for comment

words.enDefinition: Explicitly chose not to provide a statement in response to a reporter's question.

examples.en: The organizer declined to comment on the proposal after the reporter asked about the revised date.
examples.zh: 记者就提案中修改后的日期提问时，组织人员「明确拒绝置评」。

examples.en: The copy editor wrote declined to comment only after confirming that the person had actively refused.
examples.zh: 文字编辑确认当事人主动拒绝后，才使用「明确拒绝置评」的说法。

collocations: declined to comment on the proposal

words.expression: no response to a request for comment
words.lemma: no response to a request for comment
words.enDefinition: No answer received from a person or organization after a reporter requested their response.
acceptedEnVariants: no response to a request for comment
did not respond to a request for comment

examples.en: The article noted no response to a request for comment by the time it went to press.
examples.zh: 报道注明，截至截稿时仍然「征询置评未获回应」。

examples.en: We wrote that the university did not respond to a request for comment by the deadline.
examples.zh: 我们在稿件中注明，截至截稿时，向该大学「征询置评未获回应」。

collocations: note no response to a request for comment
report no response to a request for comment
record no response to a request for comment

words.enDefinition: Checking a quotation for accuracy against an interview, notes, or other reliable record.

examples.en: The editor completed quote verification by comparing the sentence with the recorded interview and the reporter's notes.
examples.zh: 编辑把句子和采访录音、记者笔记比对，完成了「引语核对」。

examples.en: We used quote verification to check the speaker's wording before fitting the sentence into the report.
examples.zh: 我们在把句子写进报道前，通过「引语核对」确认说话者的原话。

words.enDefinition: A written rendering of the words spoken during an interview.

examples.en: The interview transcript helped the reporter distinguish the organizer's actual words from a note summarizing her answer.
examples.zh: 「采访文字记录」帮助记者区分组织人员的原话与概括其回答的笔记。

examples.en: We checked the interview transcript before attributing the description to one of the two speakers.
examples.zh: 给这段描述标明是哪位发言者说的之前，我们先核对了「采访文字记录」。

words.enDefinition: A published credit showing that a story is based on someone's account as written by another person.

examples.en: The student magazine used an as told to credit for the story written from the musician's account.
examples.zh: 学生杂志用「口述经记者整理」标明该文是根据音乐人的讲述编写的。

examples.en: We discussed how as told to differed from a byline for an independent report in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们讨论了「口述经记者整理」与独立报道作者署名的区别。

collocations: publish an as told to account

words.enDefinition: An interview conducted through written questions and answers exchanged by email.

examples.en: The student reporter arranged an email interview because the organizer was unavailable during the newsroom meeting.
examples.zh: 组织人员在新闻室开会时没有空，学生记者就安排了「电子邮件采访」。

examples.en: We followed the email interview with one question asking the organizer to clarify the opening date.
examples.zh: 结束「电子邮件采访」后，我们又问了一个问题，请组织人员明确开幕日期。

words.enDefinition: An interview question inviting a developed answer in the respondent's own words.

examples.en: The reporter asked an open-ended interview question about how the workshop affected the student's daily routine.
examples.zh: 记者提了一个「开放式采访问题」，请学生谈谈工作坊怎样影响了自己的日常安排。

examples.en: We replaced the yes-or-no prompt with an open-ended interview question that invited a specific example.
examples.zh: 我们把只能答是或否的问题换成一个「开放式采访问题」，请受访者举出具体例子。

collocations: an open-ended interview question about an experience

words.enDefinition: The way a source learned the information they provide to a reporter.

examples.en: The reporter asked about the source's basis of knowledge before treating the account as firsthand information.
examples.zh: 记者先询问「消息来源的知情依据」，再决定是否把这份说法当作第一手信息。

examples.en: Our editor wanted the basis of knowledge explained so readers could evaluate the quoted claim.
examples.zh: 编辑希望文中解释「消息来源的知情依据」，让读者能够判断所引说法。

collocations: establish a source's basis of knowledge
explain a source's basis of knowledge

words.enDefinition: A newsroom unit that tests factual claims against reliable evidence.

examples.en: The fact-checking desk compared the attendance claim with the public figures and asked about a discrepancy.
examples.zh: 「事实核查组」把有关到场人数的说法与公开数据作比较，并询问两者为何不一致。

examples.en: Our fictional fact-checking desk returned the claim with a note explaining which part lacked supporting evidence.
examples.zh: 虚构「事实核查组」退回了这项说法，并附注说明哪一部分缺少佐证。

collocations: a review by the fact-checking desk
send a claim to the fact-checking desk

words.enDefinition: Checking whether material is accurate using evidence independent of its original provider.

examples.en: The editor requested independent verification because the only evidence so far came from the event organizer.
examples.zh: 由于目前唯一的证据来自活动组织人员，编辑要求进行「独立核验」。

examples.en: We used the meeting minutes for independent verification because their author had not consulted the event organizer.
examples.zh: 会议纪要的编写者没有向活动组织者征询信息，我们用这份纪要作「独立核验」。

words.enDefinition: Checking whether a picture or video accurately represents what it is claimed to show.

examples.en: The student newsroom used visual verification to check whether the supplied picture showed this year's public fair.
examples.zh: 校园新闻室通过「视觉资料核验」检查所提供的图片是否拍摄自今年的公开集市。

examples.en: Our visual verification compared the mock photograph with a publicly available image of the same building.
examples.zh: 我们进行「视觉资料核验」时，把模拟照片与同一座建筑的公开图片作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Information about an image's origin and how it reached its current form or publisher.

examples.en: The image provenance remained unclear because the picture had passed through several unrelated public accounts.
examples.zh: 图片经过几个彼此无关的公开账号流转，其「图像来源及流转」仍不明确。

examples.en: We recorded image provenance before deciding whether the picture belonged in the student article.
examples.zh: 我们先记录了「图像来源及流转」情况，再决定是否把这张图用在学生报道里。

words.enDefinition: A search using an image to find matching or visually similar images already available.

examples.en: The class used reverse image search to see whether the public campus photograph had appeared before.
examples.zh: 全班用「以图搜图」检查这张公开校园照片以前是否出现过。

examples.en: A reverse image search found the same photograph in an older public brochure for the exhibition.
examples.zh: 通过「以图搜图」，我们在一份较早的公开展览手册中找到了同一张照片。

collocations: results from a reverse image search
a reverse image search for a picture

words.enDefinition: A genuine image shown with surrounding information that misrepresents what it depicts.

examples.en: The fact-check identified an out-of-context image after finding it in a public report about a different workshop.
examples.zh: 事实核查在另一场工作坊的公开报道中找到同一张图，据此确认那是张「脱离原语境的图片」。

examples.en: Our editor rejected the out-of-context image because it did not show the event named in the draft.
examples.zh: 编辑退回了那张「脱离原语境的图片」，因为它拍的不是草稿所指的活动。

words.enDefinition: An image crop that gives an inaccurate impression by removing relevant visual context.

examples.en: The editor spotted a misleading crop when the uncropped exhibition image showed important details outside the frame.
examples.zh: 未裁切的展览照片显示，画面外还有重要细节，编辑发现这是「误导性图片裁切」。

examples.en: We explained the misleading crop by showing what the full public photograph actually included.
examples.zh: 我们展示公开原照片包含哪些内容，以说明「误导性图片裁切」造成的误解。

collocations: compare a misleading crop with the original

words.enDefinition: The first known posting of a specific item online rather than a later repost.

examples.en: The student reporters found the original upload on the public webpage for last year's campus exhibition.
examples.zh: 学生记者在去年校园展览的公开网页上找到了「最初上传版本」。

examples.en: We compared the date of the original upload with the newer date shown on the repost.
examples.zh: 我们将「最初上传版本」的日期与转发页面上较晚的日期作比较。

collocations: compare a repost with the original upload

words.enDefinition: A previously made photograph retrieved from an archive to illustrate coverage.

examples.en: The editor chose an archive photo of the reading room and clearly labeled its earlier date.
examples.zh: 编辑选了一张阅览室的「资料照片」，并清楚标出它较早的拍摄日期。

examples.en: We checked that the archive photo did not suggest that our reporters had attended the current event.
examples.zh: 我们检查「资料照片」是否会让读者误以为记者参加了这次活动。

words.enDefinition: Material made and shared by members of the public rather than by the publishing outlet.

examples.en: The newsroom checked the date and creator of user-generated content about the campus book fair before publication.
examples.zh: 刊发前，新闻室核对了有关校园书展的「用户生成内容」的日期和创作者。

examples.en: Our class asked whether the user-generated content should be used after its creator offered permission.
examples.zh: 创作者表示同意后，全班仍讨论这份「用户生成内容」是否适合用于报道。

collocations: request permission to use user-generated content

words.enDefinition: Reporting that uses quantitative or structured information as evidence to find and explain stories.

examples.en: The data journalism class studied how public library attendance changed across branches during the same period.
examples.zh: 「数据新闻」课研究了同一时期各图书馆分馆的到访量如何变化。

examples.en: We used data journalism to identify which days had the largest changes in the fictional shuttle records.
examples.zh: 我们用「数据新闻」方法从虚构接驳车记录里找出变化最大的几天。

words.enDefinition: An individual news story whose main findings or structure come from data analysis.

examples.en: The student wrote a data-driven story after noticing that evening library visits rose in the monthly totals.
examples.zh: 学生在每月统计中注意到晚间图书馆到访量上升，写出了一篇「以数据为主线的报道」。

examples.en: We backed up the data-driven story with interviews that helped explain the pattern in public figures.
examples.zh: 我们为「以数据为主线的报道」补充采访，帮助解释公开数据中的变化规律。

words.enDefinition: The documented approach used to collect, check, and interpret data for a news report.

examples.en: The editor reviewed the data reporting methodology before approving comparisons among the different fictional library branches.
examples.zh: 编辑先审查「数据报道方法」，再批准对不同虚构图书馆分馆作比较。

examples.en: We described our data reporting methodology so classmates could understand how the attendance figures were chosen.
examples.zh: 我们描述了「数据报道方法」，让同学明白所用的到场人数数据是怎样选出来的。

words.enDefinition: A request to an authority for access to records under an applicable public-access process.

examples.en: The mock public records request asked the library authority for its published budgets and meeting calendars.
examples.zh: 模拟「公开记录申请」请图书馆主管机构提供其发布的预算和会议日程。

examples.en: Our article explained which aggregate spending tables came from a public records request rather than an interview.
examples.zh: 报道说明哪些汇总支出表是经「公开记录申请」取得的，并非采访所得。

collocations: respond to a public records request

words.enDefinition: Journalism using records from public bodies as a substantive source of evidence.

examples.en: The class practiced public records reporting by comparing publicly available versions of the library's annual budget.
examples.zh: 全班比较可公开查阅的各版图书馆年度预算，练习「公共记录报道」。

examples.en: We used public records reporting to follow how the campus shuttle proposal changed before its scheduled review.
examples.zh: 我们用「公共记录报道」方法追踪校园接驳车提案在预定审议前怎样变化。

words.enDefinition: A qualification explaining a limitation that affects interpretation of reported data.

examples.en: The article included a data caveat explaining that one branch had recorded only weekday visitors.
examples.zh: 报道附上了「数据使用限制说明」，解释有一家分馆只记录了工作日访客。

examples.en: We wrote a data caveat after realizing that the figures omitted all evening workshop sessions.
examples.zh: 我们意识到这组数字遗漏了所有晚间工作坊，于是写了「数据使用限制说明」。

words.enDefinition: Checking what total or population underlies a displayed rate, share, or percentage.

examples.en: The denominator check showed that the article's percentage referred only to visitors who answered the survey.
examples.zh: 「分母核对」发现，文章中的百分比仅以回答问卷的访客为基数。

examples.en: Our editor requested a denominator check before comparing percentages from two campus branches with different reporting coverage.
examples.zh: 两家校园分馆的数据统计范围不同，编辑要求先做「分母核对」，再对比两处的百分比。

collocations: a denominator check for a percentage

words.enDefinition: An amount expressed per person or per fixed number of people in a population.

examples.en: The report used a per capita rate to compare visits in districts with different populations.
examples.zh: 报道用「按人口计算的比率」比较不同人口规模地区的到访次数。

examples.en: We checked that each per capita rate used the same population definition before comparing the districts.
examples.zh: 比较各地区前，我们核对各项「按人口计算的比率」所用的人口定义是否相同。

words.enDefinition: Documentation showing the fields, order, and structure of records in a source dataset.

examples.en: The record layout identified the column containing visit dates before the team started reading the table.
examples.zh: 小组开始读表之前，「数据记录字段布局」标出了存放到访日期的那一列。

examples.en: We reviewed the record layout to see whether the file distinguished new loans from renewals.
examples.zh: 我们审阅「数据记录字段布局」，看文件是否区分首次借阅和续借。

collocations: compare a file with its record layout

words.enDefinition: A separate section in a report outlining the sources and methods behind its findings.

examples.en: The methodology box explained where the public figures came from and how the reporter counted repeat visits.
examples.zh: 「方法说明栏」解释了公开数据来自哪里，以及记者如何统计重复到访。

examples.en: We added a methodology box beside the chart so readers could understand the two-year comparison.
examples.zh: 我们在图表旁添加「方法说明栏」，让读者看懂这项跨两年的比较。

collocations: include a methodology box with a story

words.enDefinition: A public acknowledgment and repair of a factual error in a published news report.

examples.en: The newsroom issued an editorial correction after learning that the article gave the wrong opening time.
examples.zh: 新闻室得知文章给出的开放时间有误后，发布了「报道事实更正」。

examples.en: We read the editorial correction to see which detail had changed and what the correct information was.
examples.zh: 我们读了「报道事实更正」，看哪项细节改了，以及正确消息是什么。

collocations: an editorial correction to a story

words.enDefinition: An editorial note resolving ambiguity in a previously published report.

examples.en: The editor added a clarification note explaining that the stated hours applied only to the reading room.
examples.zh: 编辑添加了「澄清说明」，解释文中所列时间只适用于阅览室。

examples.en: We used a clarification note because readers had misunderstood which branch the timetable referred to.
examples.zh: 读者误解了时间表所指的分馆，所以我们加上了「澄清说明」。

words.enDefinition: A published message from editors providing context or explaining an editorial decision.

examples.en: An editor's note explained why the student paper had combined two previously separate articles into one.
examples.zh: 「编者按」解释了学生报为何把以前分开的两篇文章合为一篇。

examples.en: We placed the editor's note above the article to explain why the original documents were linked below.
examples.zh: 我们把「编者按」放在文章上方，解释为什么原始文件的链接列在下方。

words.enDefinition: A public statement withdrawing previously published material and explaining that it should no longer be relied on.

examples.en: The fictional paper posted a retraction notice when the central claim of the article proved unsupported.
examples.zh: 文章的核心说法经查缺少依据时，虚构报纸发布了「撤稿声明」。

examples.en: We compared a retraction notice with a correction that left the rest of the student story unchanged.
examples.zh: 我们把「撤稿声明」与学生报道中只修改一处、其余内容仍保留的更正作比较。

words.enDefinition: A wire service message instructing subscribers not to use previously distributed material.

examples.en: The fictional wire service sent a kill notice after discovering that the report used the wrong document.
examples.zh: 虚构通讯社发现报道用了错误文件，随后发出「通讯社撤稿通知」。

examples.en: The exercise showed the kill notice alongside the earlier story so editors could identify the affected item.
examples.zh: 练习把「通讯社撤稿通知」与原稿放在一起，让编辑能辨认受影响的稿件。

words.enDefinition: Fixing a factual error in published news without notifying readers that the correction was made.

examples.en: The reviewer called it a silent correction because the outlet fixed a timetable error without acknowledging the change.
examples.zh: 媒体改正了时间表里的错误，却没有说明这一改动，审校人员称其为「未说明的新闻更正」。

examples.en: Our class discussed why a silent correction could confuse readers who had already shared the earlier article.
examples.zh: 全班讨论了「未说明的新闻更正」为何可能让已经分享旧版文章的读者困惑。

words.enDefinition: A note identifying new information added after a news report was first published.

examples.en: The update note said that the shuttle service had begun after the initial version of the story appeared.
examples.zh: 「新闻更新说明」写明，初版报道发布后，接驳车服务已经开通。

examples.en: We used an update note to distinguish newly confirmed details from information already in the story.
examples.zh: 我们用「新闻更新说明」区分新核实的细节和原报道已经刊出的消息。

words.enDefinition: Freedom to make editorial decisions without improper outside or commercial pressure.

examples.en: The student paper defended editorial independence when a sponsor asked to approve coverage of the campus festival.
examples.zh: 赞助方要求审定校园活动报道时，学生报维护了「编辑独立性」。

examples.en: We discussed editorial independence by looking at who had final responsibility for the publication's coverage decisions.
examples.zh: 我们查看谁对刊物的报道决定负最终责任，借此讨论「编辑独立性」。

words.enDefinition: Making the distinction between reported news and advocacy or personal opinion clear to readers.

examples.en: The redesigned labels made the separation of news and opinion clear on the newspaper's homepage.
examples.zh: 重新设计的栏目标签让读者一眼就能看出，报纸首页遵循「新闻与评论分开」的原则。

examples.en: Our class examined the separation of news and opinion by comparing an article with its accompanying column.
examples.zh: 全班把报道与配发的专栏作比较，考察「新闻与评论分开」在样刊中的做法。

collocations: maintain separation of news and opinion
a policy on separation of news and opinion
reinforce separation of news and opinion

words.enDefinition: Openness about how news was gathered, verified, presented, or corrected.

examples.en: The student publication improved editorial transparency by explaining how the public attendance numbers had been collected.
examples.zh: 学生刊物解释了公开到场人数数据的收集方式，提高了「编辑透明度」。

examples.en: We discussed editorial transparency after the newsroom added a readable explanation of its recent correction.
examples.zh: 新闻室为最近一次更正附上易读的说明后，我们讨论了「编辑透明度」。

words.enDefinition: Giving positions equal weight in coverage when the available evidence supports them unequally.

examples.en: The tutor called it false balance when the report weighed an unsupported guess equally with verified records.
examples.zh: 报道同等看待没有依据的猜测与已核实的记录，老师称之为「虚假平衡」。

examples.en: We revised the paragraph to avoid false balance while still identifying which person made the disputed claim.
examples.zh: 我们修改了段落以避免「虚假平衡」，同时明确了有争议的说法出自何人。

words.enDefinition: A published assessment of how well the evidence supports a specific factual claim.

examples.en: The fact-checking verdict explained why the quoted timetable claim was only partly supported by the public records.
examples.zh: 「事实核查结论」解释了为什么公开记录只支持所引时间表说法的一部分。

examples.en: We checked whether the fact-checking verdict referred to the precise claim investigated in the student article.
examples.zh: 我们核对「事实核查结论」所指的是否确实是学生报道调查的那项说法。
